features.name: raise the price
features.native_xml:
<roleset id="mark.04" name="raise the price" vncls="-">
<roles>
  <role descr="entity setting price" n="0" />
  <role descr="commodity" n="1" />
</roles>

<example name="transitive">
<text>
    ``On occasion, he paid a high price,'' Mr. Wachter concedes, but
    he says those who bid less and dropped out were dealers who would
    then have marked up the paintings to resell them at a profit to
    collectors. 
</text>
        <arg n="0">*trace* ->  who ->  dealers</arg>
        <arg f="MOD" n="M">would</arg>
        <arg f="TMP" n="M">then</arg>
        <rel>[ marked] [ up]</rel>
        <arg n="1">the paintings</arg>
        <arg f="PNC" n="M">to resell them at a profit to collectors</arg>
</example>

<note>
Might need other args for "amount price changed by" or "final price"
or "original price" depending on what examples appear.  If you find
such an example, send it to me.
</note>

</roleset>

  <rel>marked</rel>
  <arg n="1">his territory</arg>

<note>
I'll leave the arg3 to your imagination.
</note>

</roleset>

frame_metadata.definition: An Experiencer desires that an Event occur.  (Note that commonly a resultant state of the Event will stand in for the Event.)  In some cases, the Experiencer is an active participant in the Event, and in such cases the Event itself is often not mentioned, but rather some Focal_participant which is subordinately involved in the Event. ''Generally, the use of a word in this frame implies that the specific Event has not yet happened, but that the Experiencer believes that they would be happier if it did.  Sometimes the Time_of_event, Purpose_of_event, or the Location_of_event are mentioned without the explicit mention of the Event. 'I only wanted one piece of candy.' 'The company was eager for him to leave as soon as possible.' 'Susan really wishes that you 'd listen to her.'

warrant.reviewer: Codex primary source-backed proposal; not independent semantic gold
warrant.statement: Proposed scope: exact native noun senses with complete monetary_unit.n.01 ancestry and an explicitly attested native spelling. The 208 inspected native sense definitions and examples denote monetary units, fractional denominations, or denomination-bearing coin types. Their quantity content is intrinsic to the denomination, not the wealth or desirability of a referent. QUANTITY=+1 does not encode a particular amount, current exchange rate, size, value judgement, or ownership. A subtype whose own definition lacks quantitative denomination content falsifies this proposal. Anna (a former copper coin) and eurodollar (a deposited dollar used for international trade) are deliberately included as hard held-out audits. Morphology-derived spellings remain outside this rule until their identity is separately justified; no fallback signs apply. This is a GSE definitional projection interpreted from the native scope and measurement account, not an NSM-authored sign matrix. Source reading supports testing this proposed law; admission additionally requires independent withheld-answer model agreement across eight distinct senses and corpus replay.
